value.body:
Shape, taken as accepted (Jack Heart: "lean towards just assuming a server and then making that fast and easy"; on the eval server hosting games: "fine"; on game-process weight: "this should be solvable"). Build: every eval group runs on one Etude-owned eval process per machine that starts light game processes, owns how many are active, deadlines, failed+retry and per-match delivery; the author's InferenceServer is optional and is the only serving thing an author declares ("eval server" is not an author-facing word). Remove the separate worker-pool path and EvalJob.workers. Game-process weight: (a) a game process imports `play` from the module that defines it (play.__module__), never the experiment file unless play is defined there, and the docs example defines play in its own module; (b) Etude counts the modules each game process imports at start and, when that includes a known heavy one (torch, jax, tensorflow) or exceeds a reasonable count, reports it once, naming the module that pulled it in and the fix; pin the import count in a test. A fork server that preloads play's module is later performance work, not this PR. Performance bar: at least the 28-worker scalar CPU baseline; proving it needs a rented run, which has no allowance yet — say so in the PR.
